effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive spatial GIS and qualitative archival case study with no inferential regression point estimates; exact descriptive monetary, population, and secondary water-quality figures reported in text are included.
effect_estimate.value: Descriptive GIS/qualitative case study (no inferential regression effect estimate reported): 3 of Mebane's 4 historic African American neighborhoods (West End, White Level, and Buckhorn/Perry Hill) are excluded from municipal corporate limits while placed inside Mebane's Extraterritorial Jurisdiction (ETJ), subjecting them to municipal land-use/zoning controls without municipal voting rights or sewer service. GIS overlay of sewer lines and 2000 Census block racial data shows all 3 unincorporated African American neighborhoods lack municipal sewer access despite proximity to the sewer plant and extensions to adjacent predominantly White developments. White Level petitions for sewer service (April 7, 1997) and annexation plus sewer service (October 6, 1997; estimated cost $720,000) were refused or left unacted upon for 5 years on grounds that water/sewer are not extended outside city limits, whereas in the same October 6, 1997 session the City Council approved $268,000 in city financing to extend sewer service to newly annexed predominantly White properties. Unserved Black households rely on failing septic systems that often cannot be replaced under updated county drain-field/percolation rules, exposing properties to condemnation threats and post-rain surface water microbial contamination (cited 2002 EPA study: 5 samples each in rounds 2 and 3 exceeded EPA/NC limits for fecal coliforms, E. coli, and enterococci, with total coliphages of 1.5 to 46 infectious units/100 mL in round 3, vs. 0 of 7 samples during drought).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 7-13, Discriminatory Tactics (Racial Gerrymandering, Water Quality Critical Area, Denial of Sewer Service); Figures 2-3, PDF pp. 6, 11

sample_size.comment: No household survey or formal interview sample N is reported; empirical scope covers 1 town (Mebane, 2000 population = 7,284) and 3 excluded African American neighborhoods in its ETJ (out of 4 African American communities mapped with Census 2000 block data). Also cites a secondary 2002 EPA study of 17 surface water samples across 3 sampling rounds (7 drought, 5 round-2, 5 round-3) and 40 speakers at a June 1998 rezoning hearing.
